defects_argued.quote: The proceedings under Section 74 of the CGST Act are without jurisdiction as the SCN does not disclose the requisite ingredients of fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression of facts with intent to evade tax.

Accordingly, the mere issuance of a consolidated SCN covering multiple financial years does not constitute a patent lack of jurisdiction so as to warrant interference under Article 226 of the Constitution.

The audit proceedings and the consequential Audit Report in Form ADT-02 are vitiated since the Replies and documents furnished by the Petitioner were not considered before the audit was concluded and the SCN was issued.

The Impugned Order is liable to be set aside for failure to consider the detailed Reply submitted by the Petitioner and the documents placed on record, including DRC-03s evidencing payment/reversal of the amounts in question.

annotation.notes: Checked against full judgment, no changes. Batch order over 7 connected petitions (AVIK POLYMERS, KAMDHENU PLASTIC, SHRI BALAJI PLASTIC, SHRIRAM ENTERPRISES [this case], MANSI PLASTICS, SANJAY ENTERPRISES, R.V ENTERPRISES); the SCN (23.07.2024) and order (27.01.2025) dates are stated generically for 'the present petitions' as a group, not singled out for one lead petitioner, so unlike the JBN Impex batch (case DLHC010184962026) these are genuinely common facts, not another petitioner's. contested=false is correct and is a good example of rule 5 working as intended: this judgment applies its own precedent (Ambika Traders) and the Commercial Steel Limited SC case on writ maintainability generally, but never itself notes the Bombay HC's contrary Milroc/Rite Water line (seen in other cases in this batch) or any pending SC case on this specific point -- so despite the real conflict existing elsewhere, this judgment's own text doesn't flag it, and per rule 5 we don't import outside knowledge. consolidated_scn/defect_rejected and disposed/not-remanded (relegated to statutory appeal) both correct.
